passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis of Sysco’s financial condition, results of operations and liquidity and capital resources for the fiscal years ended June 27, 2026 and June 28, 2025 should be read as a supplement to our Consolidated Financial Statements and the accompanying notes contained in Item 8 of this report, and in conjunction with the “Forward-looking Statements” section set forth in Part II and the “Risk Factors” section set forth in Item 1A of Part I. All discussion of changes in our results of operations from fiscal 2025 to fiscal 2024 has been omitted from this Form 10-K, but may be found in Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” of our Form 10-K for the year ended June 28, 2025, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission on August 22, 2025. Overview Sysco distributes food and related products to restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments and other foodservice customers. Our primary operations are in North America and Europe. Under the accounting provisions related to disclosures about segments of an enterprise, we have combined certain operations into three reportable segments. “Other” financial information is attributable to our other operations that do not meet the quantitative disclosure thresholds. • U.S. Foodservice Operations – primarily includes (a) our U.S. Broadline operations, which distribute a full line of food products, including custom-cut meat, seafood, produce, specialty Italian, specialty imports and a wide variety of non-food products and (b) our U.S. Specialty operations, which include our FreshPoint fresh produce 32 distribution business, our Buckhead | Newport Meat & Seafood specialty protein operations, our growing Italian Specialty platform anchored by Greco & Sons, Inc., our Edward Don restaurant equipment and supplies distribution business, our Asian specialty distribution company and a number of other small specialty businesses that are not material to the operations of Sysco; • International Foodservice Operations – includes operations outside of the United States (U.S.), which distribute a full line of food products and a wide variety of non-food products. The Americas primarily consists of operations in Canada, Bahamas, Costa Rica and Panama, as well as our export operations that distribute to international customers. Our European operations primarily consist of operations in the United Kingdom (U.K.), France, Ireland and Sweden; • SYGMA – our U.S. customized distribution operations serving quick-service chain restaurant customer locations; and • Other – primarily our hotel supply operations, Guest Worldwide. We estimate that we serve about 18% of an approximately $377 billion annual foodservice market in the U.S. based on industry data obtained from Technomic, Inc. (Technomic) as of the end of calendar year 2025. Technomic projects the market size to increase to approximately $390 billion by the end of calendar year 2026. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: The following discussion of “risk factors” identifies the most significant factors that may adversely affect our business, results of operations, financial position and future financial performance. This information should be read in conjunction with Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations and the consolidated financial statements and related notes contained in this report. The following discussion of risks is not all inclusive but is designed to highlight what we believe are the most significant factors to consider when evaluating our business. These factors could cause our future results to differ from our expectations expressed in the forward-looking statements identified within “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and from other historical trends. Risk Factor Summary The following is a summary of the principal risks that could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and cash flows, or the value of our securities. This summary does not describe all of the risks we face and should be read together with the more detailed discussion of the risk factors set forth below in this Item 1A and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us, or that we currently deem immaterial, may also impair our business. Industry and General Economic Risks • Our industry is characterized by low margins, and periods of significant or prolonged inflation or deflation affect our product costs and may negatively impact our profitability and results of operations. • A shortage of qualified labor and increases in labor costs could adversely affect our business and materially reduce earnings. • Global health developments and economic uncertainty resulting from global public health crises may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. • Unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, as well as unfavorable conditions in particular local markets, may adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. • We may not be able to fully compensate for increases in fuel costs, and fuel hedging arrangements intended to contain fuel costs could result in above market fuel costs, any of which could adversely affect our results of operations. • Economic and political instability and changes in laws and regulations could adversely affect our results of operations and financial condition. • Competition and the impact of GPOs may reduce our margins and make it difficult for us to maintain our market share, growth rate and profitability. credit_strengths.text: Sysco's scale as the largest North American foodservice distributor, serving roughly a fifth of a very large addressable market, underpins revenue growth that has compounded across the three-year trend even as operating income flattened, evidencing resilient demand and pricing power in a low-margin industry.

Operating cash flow covers capital spending comfortably, leaving free cash flow that funds shareholder distributions and modest acquisitions, while cash on hand and a current ratio above the sector median provide a liquidity cushion against working-capital swings typical of food distribution.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage flags low industry margins and significant or prolonged inflation or deflation as pressures on product costs and profitability; operating margin sits well below the sector median, so cost pass-through failures would compress already thin earnings and weaken coverage.

Debt maturities cluster in the near term, with a large tranche due within twelve months and further repayments in each of the following years, so refinancing risk is meaningful; leverage sits above the sector median and only modest EBITDA erosion would breach the next threshold.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage remains adequate but below the sector median, and cash interest paid is used as a proxy because no income-statement interest expense tag was reported; this data gap is material because capitalized interest is not interest expense and coverage could be overstated.

Free cash flow to debt is modest and well below the sector median, while dividends and buybacks absorb most free cash flow, leaving limited retained cash for deleveraging; net leverage is near the downgrade threshold, so cash-flow durability is central to the servicing view.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is Significant, driven by leverage above the sector median and cash-flow coverage in a lower tier; the trend shows debt rising faster than EBITDA, and shareholder returns consume most free cash flow, so deleveraging depends on earnings recovery rather than retained cash.

Our forward view is that credit quality is stable but sensitive to margin pressure and refinancing conditions; the near-term maturity wall and thin headroom to the next leverage threshold mean a modest EBITDA decline or debt-funded distribution could weaken the profile, warranting close monitoring.

credit_strengths.text: Sysco作為北美最大食品服務分銷商的規模，服務於一個非常龐大潛在市場的約五分之一，支撐了收入增長，該增長在三年趨勢中複合上升，即使營業收入持平，證明在低利潤行業中需求具韌性及定價能力。
營運現金流輕鬆覆蓋資本支出，留下自由現金流用於資助股東分派及適度收購，而手頭現金及流動比率高於行業中位數，為食品分銷典型的營運資金波動提供流動性緩衝。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落指出行業利潤率低及顯著或持續的通脹或通縮對產品成本及盈利能力的壓力；營業利潤率遠低於行業中位數，因此成本轉嫁失敗將壓縮本已微薄的盈利並削弱覆蓋率。
債務到期集中在近期，其中一大筆將於十二個月內到期，隨後各年亦有進一步還款，因此再融資風險重大；槓桿高於行業中位數，僅需溫和的EBITDA侵蝕便會突破下一門檻。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率仍屬充足但低於行業中位數，由於未報告損益表利息費用標籤，故以已付現金利息作為代理；此數據缺口屬重大，因為資本化利息並非利息費用，覆蓋率可能被高估。
自由現金流對債務比率適中且遠低於行業中位數，而股息及回購吸收大部分自由現金流，留下有限留存現金用於去槓桿；淨槓桿接近降級門檻，因此現金流持久性對償債觀點至關重要。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為顯著，受槓桿高於行業中位數及現金流覆蓋率處於較低層級所驅動；趨勢顯示債務增長快於EBITDA，且股東回報消耗大部分自由現金流，因此去槓桿取決於盈利復甦而非留存現金。
我們的前瞻觀點是信貸質量穩定但對利潤率壓力及再融資條件敏感；近期到期牆及對下一槓桿門檻的微薄緩衝意味著溫和的EBITDA下降或債務融資分派可能削弱狀況，值得密切監測。
